name: phoenix

platform.name: Unknown
platform.why: the Dockerfile builds a release image that the workflows push to GHCR; terraform-e2e.yml manages uptime checks, not hosting; nothing names a host

processes.what: Phoenix release (with Oban queues and cron in the same BEAM)
processes.note: ENTRYPOINT rel/docker-entrypoint.sh, CMD run -> /app/bin/plausible start on :8000; the Oban queues, the Oban cron plugin, the event write buffer and the cache refreshers all run inside this one node (lib/plausible/application.ex)

data.note: Plausible.Repo on DATABASE_URL; also the Oban job table and the Oban peer election
CLICKHOUSE_DATABASE_URL: the events and sessions store (Plausible.IngestRepo, priv/ingest_repo)

VOLUME /var/lib/plausible as DEFAULT_DATA_DIR: CSV imports and exports while S3_DISABLED is true (the default in config/runtime.exs), the geolocation and tzdata caches, the session transfer socket, the self-hosted TLS certificates (site_encrypt)

breaks.note: Oban queues on Postgres (imports, exports, email reports and more; workers in lib/workers/) run inside the web node and need CPU between requests; no Elixir rule exists for it
Oban.Plugins.Cron with base_cron (salt rotation daily, email reports hourly, traffic notifier every 15 minutes, ...) and the Reindexer schedule, all inside the node
events are held in memory and flushed to ClickHouse on a Process.send_after tick; with CPU throttled after the request the flush waits, and an instance stopped hard loses the buffer
warmed caches (sites, shield rules, tracker scripts) refresh on intervals of 25 s to 1 min
the salt cache is refreshed by a timer inside the node
mv! (File.rename!/File.cp!) is the write behind uploads and exports kept on local disk
with storage "local" an uploaded CSV is moved into DATA_DIR/plausible-imports for a later Oban job, which may run on another instance
the export archive is written into DATA_DIR/plausible-exports and downloaded later

visitor sessions of the analytics are kept in an in-memory cache per node (Plausible.Cache :sessions, Session.Balancer); several instances count one visitor as several sessions. Not login sessions; no Elixir rule exists for it

idle.note: socket "/live" Phoenix.LiveView.Socket: LiveView pages (imports, settings, SSO) hold a websocket

a developer mix task that writes plan files
the browser tracking script, a setInterval in the visitor's page; tracker/ is not excluded by the node rules
browser code injected to verify an installation
the build script that compiles tracker variants into priv/tracker/js

a GenServer that refreshes a cached cluster version; a stalled refresh between requests costs nothing

notes: Read the Dockerfile, rel/ (entrypoint and overlay scripts), config/runtime.exs, lib/plausible/application.ex, the ingestion and session modules, the endpoint and the Elixir and Node rule hits. Everything runs in one BEAM release: splitting the Oban queues and cron from the web node, or moving cron to Cloud Scheduler, is the main change, and the ClickHouse write buffer plus the per-node session cache assume one long-lived node (the release even hands the session cache over through DATA_DIR on redeploys). Migrations are rel/overlays/migrate.sh, started by `db migrate` through the entrypoint by hand or by an outside compose file, not by a release step in this repository. The self-hosted HTTPS (site_encrypt, certbot in the CE image) is not needed behind Cloud Run. Only local-disk-write has an Elixir rule, so most breaks here have no regex today.
